task.name: Post-run findings carry no bug type, so intake adds feature-only refusals to intentionally untriaged findings
task.story_text:
## Observed

Every finding the post-run hook files is a bug report, and none of them is labelled as one.

A hook-filed finding arrives with `forge-finding`, `p2`, `needs-triage` — no type label. With
no recognized type the shape gate classifies it as a feature and demands acceptance criteria
and a worked example from a defect report, so it refuses:

```
blocking  missing_type                 Issue has no recognized type label
blocking  missing_acceptance_criteria  No acceptance criteria section found
blocking  no_observable_done_state     No acceptance criteria section
blocking  untriaged_finding            finding still has needs-triage label
```

The body itself is fine: adding the `bug` label and removing the feature sections a later
groom pass scaffolded in returns `RUNNABLE` with no other change. Only the type was ever
missing.

`needs-triage` is a deliberate lifecycle state and is expected to hold a finding out of a
sprint until it is triaged; that part works as designed. The defect is the missing type, and
the feature-shaped refusals that follow from it — a finding should be held for triage, not
held for lacking acceptance criteria it will never have.

The hook files one issue per P1/P2 review finding, so these accumulate at roughly the rate
stories complete.

## Expected

A component that files issues declares their type at creation, so the gate classifies them
as what they are rather than inferring a type from a body format the component also chose.
Review findings are defect reports and are typed as such.


## Diagnosis

**Baseline:** `e4d80220bd3699b40fe3a0d9e043e824b3a74168` captured at `2026-08-23T14:22:24.941760+00:00`

**Inspected files:**

- `forge.yaml` — `sha256:3c80f3cf3696c9ed692dd5e6849d9f82883a161c5fd7fd8fa5dd4d1154eb9927`
- `.forge/hooks/post_run.sh` — `sha256:2614bbdee5e21536a793a2bbbfee6b9a163b595cf89f779c29de4e974f9017c2`
- `.forge/hooks/post-run-gh-issues.sh` — `sha256:bc893075450f89f0880750452004956d9b0ab835b3ebf8e8eb1d4a964c648361`
- `src/theforge/shape_check/heuristics.py` — `sha256:7d77f749c73ee947103ad4a7030e9fd433088e13106df04fc38aa48727847442`
- `src/theforge/shape_check/parsing.py` — `sha256:f0e4b272622e7a0b3a9ae7f42360a06611e659798e1492ae42c294d707a8f2f6`
- `src/theforge/shape_check/check.py` — `sha256:fab737d9c2977b71fe4fa471c5fd188c1833fd1af0d3aae97fb2f5aa88c8b013`

### Observed symptom

Every GitHub issue that the post-run hook automatically files for a P1/P2
review finding is refused at intake by the shape gate. The gate reports
blocking `missing_type`, `missing_acceptance_criteria`, `no_observable_done_state`,
and `untriaged_finding` — treating a well-formed defect report as a malformed
feature request because nothing in the issue declares it is a bug.

### Reproduction / evidence

Read forge.yaml:336 — `post_run: .forge/hooks/post_run.sh` — confirming this
is the hook forge actually wires up (not the alternate
.forge/hooks/post-run-gh-issues.sh, which was also inspected and has the
same defect independently).

Read .forge/hooks/post_run.sh lines 75-80: the `gh issue create` call that
files one issue per finding applies exactly three labels —
`--label "forge-finding" --label "needs-triage" --label "$(echo "$sev" | tr 'A-Z' 'a-z')"`
(severity, e.g. "p2") — and never applies `bug`, `enhancement`, `epic`, or
`task`.

Read src/theforge/shape_check/heuristics.py:
- `check_missing_type` (line 729) computes
  `_lower_labels(labels) & _RECOGNIZED_TYPE_LABELS` where
  `_RECOGNIZED_TYPE_LABELS = frozenset({"bug", "enhancement", "epic", "task"})`
  (line 139). With none of those labels present, `matches` is empty and the
  function returns the blocking `missing_type` Reason.
- `is_bug_format_issue` (line 718) returns true only if `_BUG_LABELS &
  labels` is non-empty (i.e. the `bug` label is present) OR
  `has_bug_body_headings(body)` is true. `has_bug_body_headings`
  (src/theforge/shape_check/parsing.py:321-329) requires actual Markdown
  headings matching `what happened|observed|actual behaviou?r` paired with
  `what was expected|expected`, or a `steps to reproduce` heading. The
  hook's body (post_run.sh lines 54-58) writes
  `**Observed:** ${observed}` / `**Expected:** ${expected}` /
  `**Evidence:** ${evidence}` as bold inline prose, not as `## Observed` /
  `## Expected` Markdown headings, so `has_heading()` never matches and
  `is_bug_format_issue` returns False.
- With `is_bug_format_issue` False, `check_missing_acceptance_criteria`
  (line 950) and `check_no_observable_done_state` (line 1304) both skip
  their bug-format exemption and evaluate the body as a feature, finding no
  `## Acceptance Criteria` section — hence the two additional blocking
  reasons.
- `check_untriaged_finding` (line 1051) fires independently because the
  hook always applies `needs-triage`, and the shape rules require an
  operator to remove it after triage — but triage itself is unreachable
  while the same issue is also refused for `missing_type`.
- src/theforge/shape_check/check.py:59-77 runs all checks unconditionally
  and collects every Reason rather than short-circuiting on the first
  blocking one, which is why all four codes appear together in the
  reported gate output, exactly as the issue's "Observed" section shows.

### Hypotheses tested

- **[ruled out]** The shape gate's classifier has a code defect that misreads a correctly-typed bug label.
  - Evidence: check_missing_type's logic is a straightforward set-intersection against a correct RECOGNIZED_TYPE_LABELS constant; the issue's own diagnosis (and this investigation) confirms that adding 'bug' plus removing the two scaffolded feature sections makes the same body pass (RUNNABLE). The classifier behaves correctly given its inputs — the inputs (labels) are what's missing.
  - Evidence provenance: observed — directly observed during this investigation. Verified directly against heuristics.py at HEAD.
- **[confirmed]** The post_run hook never applies a recognized type label (bug/enhancement/epic/task) when filing findings, so check_missing_type always fires, and the absence of a type label also makes is_bug_format_issue fall back to feature-shape checks (acceptance criteria / observable done state) that a bug body cannot satisfy.
  - Evidence: post_run.sh's gh issue create call (lines 75-80) applies only forge-finding, needs-triage, and the lowercased severity — never a type label. heuristics.py's is_bug_format_issue requires either the 'bug' label or heading-shaped (## Observed / ## Expected) content; the hook writes bold-inline **Observed:** prose instead of headings, so neither path is satisfied and the body is evaluated as a feature.
  - Evidence provenance: observed — directly observed during this investigation. All four files read directly at HEAD in this investigation; not a restatement of the issue's own diagnosis, though the issue's manual repair experiment (typing #2690 by hand) independently corroborates the same mechanism.
- **[ruled out]** The alternate hook file .forge/hooks/post-run-gh-issues.sh (a differently-shaped, non-wired script) is the one actually responsible.
  - Evidence: forge.yaml:336 wires post_run to .forge/hooks/post_run.sh specifically; post-run-gh-issues.sh is not referenced by any config key. It happens to share the identical defect (no type label applied), but it is not the active hook.
  - Evidence provenance: observed — directly observed during this investigation. Read forge.yaml directly.

### Confirmed cause

The post-run hook (.forge/hooks/post_run.sh, wired via forge.yaml's
`post_run` key), when filing one GitHub issue per P1/P2 review finding,
applies only the labels `forge-finding`, `needs-triage`, and a lowercased
severity (e.g. `p2`) — it never applies a recognized type label (`bug`,
`enhancement`, `epic`, or `task`). Because the shape gate's
`check_missing_type` requires exactly one label from that recognized set,
every hook-filed finding is blocked with `missing_type`. Compounding this,
the gate's `is_bug_format_issue` helper (which several other checks consult
to grant the bug-shape exemption) also requires either the `bug` label or
Markdown-heading-shaped Observed/Expected sections; the hook writes its
Observed/Expected/Evidence fields as bold inline prose (`**Observed:** ...`)
rather than as `## Observed` headings, so the exemption is denied on both
paths. With no type label and no heading-recognized bug shape, the gate
falls through to evaluating the issue as a feature, additionally blocking
it for `missing_acceptance_criteria` and `no_observable_done_state`.

Support: Directly read the wired hook script's `gh issue create` invocation (labels
applied) and the shape gate's `check_missing_type` / `is_bug_format_issue`
/ `check_missing_acceptance_criteria` / `check_no_observable_done_state`
source, and traced the exact label set and body format the hook produces
against the exact conditions those checks require. This is independent
confirmation via source reading, not merely a restatement of the issue's
own diagnosis — though the issue's own manual-repair experiment (typing
#2690 as `bug` and stripping scaffolded sections yields RUNNABLE) is
consistent with and corroborates the same mechanism.
Support provenance: observed — directly observed during this investigation. All claims verified by direct source inspection in this investigation.
Independence note: This text uses independence/corroboration language. Verify the cited material is a second source rather than a prior assertion.

### Premise verification

> The coordinator could not verify the following cited premises against the baseline.

- `forge/hooks/post_run.sh` — unable to check: file absent at baseline but no removing commit could be identified

### Affected code path

.forge/hooks/post_run.sh (the gh issue create call around lines 75-80, and
the body-construction block around lines 54-58) — the finding-creation path
that supplies the label set and body format for every hook-filed issue.

### Fix-success criterion

A finding the hook files is created carrying its type, so the gate classifies it as a bug
and the only reasons holding it out of a sprint are lifecycle ones appropriate to a finding
— triage, and where required diagnosis. Refusals that follow from being misread as a feature
no longer occur.

### Related findings (out of scope)

> These are adjacent problems noticed during investigation. They are **not** the cause of this issue's symptom and are **out of scope for this fix** — triage them separately under the linked issue. Do not implement them as part of this issue.

- The unwired reference script .forge/hooks/post-run-gh-issues.sh has the identical missing-type-label defect in its own gh issue create call; harmless while unwired but a latent trap if ever adopted as the active hook.
- The shape gate's missing_type refusal message, when a body is otherwise bug-shaped content typed as a feature by default, tells the reader to add acceptance criteria/example sections that don't belong on a bug — this is the 'refusal names the consequences of an assumed type rather than the missing attribute' behavior the issue's Expected section calls out, and is a gate-behavior concern separate from the hook's label omission, and belongs to the shared-evaluation work rather than to this fix.

### Stated symptom scope coverage

The hook files one issue per P1/P2 review finding, so these accumulate at roughly the rate stories complete — every hook-filed finding is affected, not one instance.

- **[covered]** .forge/hooks/post_run.sh:75-80 (gh issue create for review findings)
  - Rationale: This is the wired post_run hook per forge.yaml:336; its single finding-creation call path is the sole site filing these issues, so covering it covers the full categorical population.
- **[excluded]** .forge/hooks/post-run-gh-issues.sh:20-31 (alternate, unwired gh issue create)
  - Rationale: Not referenced by forge.yaml or any other config key found via grep; not part of the live finding-creation path today. Recorded as related_findings instead since it shares the defect but is not currently exercised.

### Notes

The alternate script .forge/hooks/post-run-gh-issues.sh is not wired by
forge.yaml and is out of scope for this issue's fix, but it carries the
identical omission (no type label in its gh issue create call, lines
20-31) — recorded below as a related finding since it would reproduce the
same failure if it were ever wired up or used as a reference elsewhere.

This diagnosis intentionally does not prescribe which label the hook
should apply or how the shape gate's fallback-refusal wording should
change (the issue's Expected section asks for both: label at creation, and
a refusal that names the missing type rather than the consequences of an
assumed one) — that is fix-design scope, not diagnosis scope.
